scope.description: Pre-commit queue transition for a retained request on a nonsingleton leader, including commitment triggered by applying an already committed configuration. Synchronous Ready/Advance caller using the documented early-Advance optimization; actual application remains ordered.
assumptions: Serialized RawNode methods, authentic peer messages and a stable leader during the measured transition.
Ready entries/HardState are persisted before Advance and messages; actual committed-entry application remains in log order.
The explicit package/Node permission to Advance after persistence while application is in progress applies through RawNode's documented correspondence to Node.
Unique request contexts, ReadOnlySafe, no process or storage crash.
excluded: Unconditional public ReadIndex completion; requests can be lost per API.
A time bound or general liveness result.
Linearizability violation, lease-based reads, concurrent context reuse and joint-configuration exhaustive coverage.

properties.reason: Independent applicability, correlated prerequisites and fully observed result comparison

adaptations: Only a package-local test is added; target protocol and dependencies are unchanged.
MemoryStorage and deterministic caller worker/network scheduling replace an unspecified deployment backend under a no-crash scope.
The explicit early-Advance optimization is selected: one committed configuration is persisted/advanced before its ApplyConfChange; later application is kept in order.
Unexported protocol state is read for observations and setup checks, with no direct critical-state writes.
Normal commands are no-op application payloads; Ready read results are recorded, not interpreted as a client state-machine reply.
All state-mutating protocol calls use Node. Status rendezvous synchronize observations; package-local RawNode access only reads readiness and protocol state. No substitute run loop is used.

plan_uncertainties: This is a documented internal queue-transition requirement, not an unconditional public ReadIndex completion guarantee.
Applicability includes the explicit synchronous early-Advance interpretation; RawNode shorthand and general loss allowance remain visible for review.
No time bound, stale-read result, crash scenario or deployment performance claim is checked.
The later proposal control is an attributed diagnostic endpoint for the same request, not part of admission or the oracle.
grounding_unresolved: A stricter interpretation requiring configuration activation before early Advance would exclude this prefix; correspondence review must adjudicate that interpretation from the captured API documentation.
Semantic review must judge the early-Advance interpretation and narrow internal queue expectation; no claim of general read liveness follows from execution.
Whether the public early-Advance optimization extends to deferred ApplyConfChange remains explicit in the accepted scope.

blockers: Open review issue 273fb925e4b943d299768ea5bbade258 [S_api,S_node_advance_order,S_raw_advance_contract,S_early_advance_usage,S_early_advance_readme,S_read_api_contract,S_pending_read_purpose]: S_raw_advance_contract describes completed application for the API actually called; S_node_advance_order and S_early_advance_usage explicitly permit the optimization for Node.

S_raw_advance_contract describes Advance as applied-and-saved, whereas S_early_advance_usage and S_node_advance_order permit Advance before application finishes. The scope adopts the explicit optimization permission and keeps this documentation tension visible.

RawNode.Advance describes applied-and-saved completion. The check adopts the explicit Node/package early-Advance optimization; if a stricter configuration-specific ordering is required, this prefix is excluded.
